content.en: National Investment & Manufacturing Zones (NIMZ) are a key policy instrument under the **National Manufacturing Policy (NMP)**. These zones are conceived as self-contained industrial townships with world-class infrastructure, land use on a long-term basis, and clean, energy-efficient technology. They aim to create an ecosystem where manufacturing can thrive by reducing regulatory burdens and providing high-quality logistics.

definition.en: Provision of internal and external connectivity, power, water, and waste management systems.
definition.hi: Provision of internal and external connectivity, power, water, and waste management systems.

content.en: Each NIMZ is managed by a Special Purpose Vehicle to ensure administrative autonomy and efficient decision-making.
content.hi: Each NIMZ is managed by a Special Purpose Vehicle to ensure administrative autonomy and efficient decision-making.

content.en: Do not confuse NIMZs with SEZs; NIMZs are focused on manufacturing and industrial growth rather than purely export-oriented trade.
content.hi: Do not confuse NIMZs with SEZs; NIMZs are focused on manufacturing and industrial growth rather than purely export-oriented trade.

content.en: Focus on how NIMZs align with the 'Ease of Doing Business' framework in India.
content.hi: Focus on how NIMZs align with the 'Ease of Doing Business' framework in India.

keyTakeaways.en: NIMZs are designed to increase the share of manufacturing in GDP.

keyTakeaways.en: They function as industrial townships with integrated infrastructure.
